sourcedFrom: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) (2022 (© 2022 ADVANCED ARMAMENT CO. / © 2022 JJE Brands, LLC.))
cleanIntro: This guide follows AAC's TM-RANGER SERIES technical manual (105116 REV-10.22). That book covers the whole Ranger series and never prints "Ranger 7", so check your variant against it. The Ranger is a welded stainless and Inconel rifle silencer with a 1-3/8-24 threaded socket at the rear, which takes either a fast-attach mount or a direct-thread mount, and a removable front-end cap. The maintenance AAC publishes is short: off the rifle and cold, mount out, front-end cap out, scrub the threaded sockets and tapers at both ends, clean the cap and mount threads, then grease and refit both. The book gives no way into the welded core and goes no further than the mount and the cap.

steps.title: Make the HOST rifle safe first: magazine out, empty, on SAFE
steps.action: This guide follows AAC's Ranger Series manual, which does not name the Ranger 7 by number, so check your variant against it. Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction. Remove the magazine, unload the rifle completely and put its safety on "SAFE", following the rifle's own manual.
steps.prose: This book covers the silencer, not the rifle it sits on. The silencer has no action to clear, and for unloading the rifle AAC sends you to that rifle's own owner's manual.
steps.quote: 2. Render the firearm safe by removing the magazine, completely unloading the firearm and engaging the safety mechanism to the "SAFE" position. See the firearm's owner's manual for detailed instructions.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Removing a RANGER SERIES silencer configured for fast-attach use from a host firearm, step 2, P.10
steps.warn: Never install or remove a silencer on or from a host firearm that you have not verified to be completely empty and rendered safe.

steps.title: Let it cool to ambient before you touch it
steps.action: Check that the silencer has cooled to ambient temperature, and let it cool if it is still hot. If it has to come off hot, wear heat-resistant gloves.
steps.prose: A silencer that has just been shot looks exactly like a cold one, and it is hot enough to burn a bare hand.
steps.quote: 3. Verify the silencer is at ambient temperature. If the silencer is hot, allow it to cool.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Removing a RANGER SERIES silencer configured for fast-attach use from a host firearm, step 3, P.10
steps.warn: Never handle a hot silencer without heat-resistant gloves, as this may lead to skin burns and/or personal injury.

steps.title: Fast-attach: hold the latch thumb pad down and unscrew
steps.action: If your Ranger is on a fast-attach mount, grip it firmly by the mount. Press and hold the textured thumb pad on the ratchet latch, and unscrew the silencer off the BLACKOUT muzzle device. Keep the thumb pad held down the whole time you turn it.
steps.prose: AAC's fast-attach mount carries a ratchet latch with a textured thumb pad. The book has you hold that pad down both when screwing the silencer on and when taking it off.
steps.quote: 4. While firmly grasping the mount, depress and hold the textured thumb-pad on the ratchet latch and unscrew the silencer from the BLACKOUT Silencer-Mounting muzzle device in the direction indicated in Figure 16.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Removing a RANGER SERIES silencer configured for fast-attach use from a host firearm, step 4, P.10

steps.title: Direct-thread: grip the mount and unscrew it off the muzzle
steps.action: If your Ranger is on a direct-thread mount, the same two checks come first: the rifle empty and on SAFE, and the can cool. Then grip it firmly by the direct-thread mount and unscrew it off the muzzle threads.
steps.prose: A direct-thread mount has no latch. It is held by its threads and by the mount sitting square against the barrel's shoulder.
steps.quote: unscrew the silencer from the muzzle threads in the direction indicated in Figure 22.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Removing a RANGER SERIES silencer configured for direct-thread use from a host firearm, step 4, P.12

steps.title: Take the mount out of the rear of the silencer
steps.action: With the silencer off the rifle, remove whichever mount is installed. Break a fast-attach mount loose with a spanner, or a direct-thread mount with a 3/4" socket. Then unthread it the rest of the way by hand.
steps.prose: AAC's cleaning section starts here, because the threaded socket and tapered sealing surface it scrubs are behind the mount. Mount changes are made only with the silencer off a rifle.
steps.quote: If there is a fast-attach or direct thread mount installed, remove the mount following the instructions in this manual.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 1, P.13
steps.warn: Only perform configuration changes on silencers that are not mounted to a firearm.

steps.title: Remove the front-end cap
steps.action: Remove the front-end cap from the front of the silencer. It is a threaded insert, so you reach the front threaded socket and taper by taking it out.
steps.prose: AAC describes the front-end cap inserts as removable and replaceable if they are damaged, so look the cap over as it comes out.
steps.quote: Remove the front-end cap from the silencer.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 2, P.13

steps.title: Field strip complete: the core stays welded
steps.action: The silencer is off the rifle, the mount is out of the rear and the front-end cap is out of the front. That is as far as AAC's book goes. The baffle core is welded and the book gives no way into it. The scrubbing and refitting AAC describes are under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Everything the book cleans is a thread or a sealing taper: the sockets at each end, the cap threads and the mount threads and taper.
steps.quote: The RANGER SERIES are constructed of fully laser welded 17-4 stainless steel and Inconel 718 for light-weight and durability.
steps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — General description, P.3
steps.warn: Only perform cleaning and maintenance procedures on silencers that are not mounted to a firearm and are at ambient temperature.

deepSteps.title: Scrub the REAR threaded socket and taper
deepSteps.action: With a gun cleaning brush and solvent, scrub the threaded socket and the tapered sealing surface in the rear of the silencer thoroughly. Wear eye protection and solvent-resistant gloves, and work in a well-ventilated place away from open flame.
deepSteps.prose: The mount seats on this taper. AAC warns never to fit a mount into threads or a taper that are dirty or damaged.
deepSteps.quote: Using a gun cleaning brush and solvent, thoroughly scrub the threaded socket and taper in the rear of the silencer.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 3, P.13
deepSteps.warn: Always wear protective gear, such as eye protection and solvent-resistant gloves when working with any solvent.

deepSteps.title: Scrub the FRONT threaded socket and taper
deepSteps.action: Do the same at the front, where the front-end cap seats. Scrub the threaded socket and the taper thoroughly with the brush and solvent.
deepSteps.prose: The front socket gets the same brush and solvent as the rear, before the cap goes back in.
deepSteps.quote: Using a gun cleaning brush and solvent, thoroughly scrub the threaded socket and taper in the front of the silencer.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 4, P.13

deepSteps.title: Clean the front-end cap's threads
deepSteps.action: Clean the threads on the outside of the front-end cap.
deepSteps.prose: Do this before the cap gets its fresh grease, so the grease goes onto clean threads.
deepSteps.quote: Clean the threads on the outside of the front-end cap.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 5, P.13

deepSteps.title: Clean the mount's threads and taper
deepSteps.action: Clean the threads and the taper on the outside of the fast-attach or direct-thread mount, and check them for damage as you go.
deepSteps.prose: The mount's outer taper is the other half of the seal you scrubbed in the rear socket. Both halves need to be clean for the mount to seat true.
deepSteps.quote: Clean the threads and taper on the outside of the fast-attach or direct thread mount.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 6, P.13

deepSteps.title: Grease the cap threads and refit the front-end cap
deepSteps.action: Put a small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on the front-end cap's threads, then screw the cap back into the front of the silencer.
deepSteps.prose: AAC asks for a small amount, and names either high-temperature grease or anti-seize.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a small amount of high temperature grease or anti-seize to the threads on the front-end cap and reinstall the front end cap in the front of the silencer.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 7, P.13

deepSteps.title: Grease the mount's threads and taper and refit the mount
deepSteps.action: Put a small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on the mount's threads and taper. Thread it into the rear until its taper seats against the taper inside the silencer, then tighten it: a fast-attach mount with a spanner, a direct-thread mount with a 3/4" socket.
deepSteps.prose: The two tapers meeting is what tells you the mount is home. The book's configuration pages name the spanner for the fast-attach mount and the 3/4" socket for the direct-thread mount.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a small amount of high temperature grease or anti-seize to the threads and taper on the fast-attach or direct thread mount
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 8, P.13

deepSteps.title: Wipe the outside clean
deepSteps.action: Wipe off the outside of the silencer with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.prose: That is the last step of AAC's cleaning procedure.
deepSteps.quote: 9. Wipe off the exterior of the silencer with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.cite: TM-RANGER SERIES — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL RANGER SERIES — 105116 REV-10.22 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning the RANGER SERIES, step 9, P.14

cleaning.name: OFF THE RIFLE, COLD
tasks: Host rifle: magazine out, fully unloaded, on SAFE
Silencer at ambient temperature, or heat-resistant gloves on
Fast-attach: thumb pad held down while unscrewing; direct-thread: gripped by the mount
Do not clean or change the mount while the silencer is on a rifle

cleaning.name: MOUNT AND FRONT-END CAP
tasks: Mount broken loose (spanner for fast-attach, 3/4" socket for direct-thread) and unthreaded by hand
Front-end cap removed from the front of the silencer
Cap and mount looked over for damage

cleaning.name: SCRUB
tasks: Rear threaded socket and taper scrubbed with a gun cleaning brush and solvent
Front threaded socket and taper scrubbed with a gun cleaning brush and solvent
Front-end cap threads cleaned
Mount threads and taper cleaned
Eye protection, solvent-resistant gloves, ventilation, no open flame

cleaning.name: GREASE AND REFIT
tasks: Small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on the cap threads; cap refitted
Small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on the mount threads and taper
Mount threaded in until the tapers seat, then tightened
Exterior wiped with a clean cloth

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No auxiliary thread adapter between the barrel and a BLACKOUT muzzle device
⛔ No crush washer or compression washer when installing a BLACKOUT muzzle device
⛔ Never fit a mount into threads or a taper that are dirty or damaged
⛔ Never shoot through a silencer with an obstructed bore

reassembly: Mount refitted in the rear (greased threads and taper, seated taper to taper, then tightened), and the front-end cap refitted in the front.

Fast-attach: the BLACKOUT muzzle device's threads, the toothed gear behind them and the alignment surfaces checked clean and undamaged, and the mount designation checked as compatible with the muzzle device. Direct-thread: the muzzle threads and shoulder cleaned and checked, any flash hider, washers or shims removed, and the mount's thread specification checked against the muzzle.
Looked through from the rear to confirm the bullet path is clear, and the silencer checked for any damage.

Fast-attach: slid over the muzzle device and screwed on hand-tight with the thumb pad held down, then the thumb pad released. Direct-thread: screwed on until the rear of the mount sits flush and square against the shoulder behind the threads.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and on SAFE and the silencer cool: look through the silencer from the rear and confirm the bullet path is clear. Fast-attach: with the thumb pad released there should be no perceptible movement between the muzzle device and the silencer. Do not over-tighten it, or it may be hard to remove. Direct-thread: the rear of the mount should sit flush and square against the barrel's shoulder. AAC makes the user responsible for keeping the silencer securely threaded during use, and its bore must line up with the bore of the barrel it is on.
